Hewlett Packard Enterprise Falls 5% as AI Financing Worries Extend Hardware Selloff; Super Micro Sinks 7%, Dell Drops 3%
AI hardware stocks are cracking under a debate investors cannot yet resolve: who actually pays for the data center buildout, and whether the revenue surge was ever what it seemed.
Published October 16, 2026, 11:42am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Worries over how the AI infrastructure boom gets paid for are rippling through hardware stocks again. Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) stock is down 5% at $55.87 this morning, extending a selloff that has swept across the biggest names in AI servers.
Meanwhile, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 7% to $32.78, a larger slide than Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock. Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is down 3% to $458.78, a softer decline than Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock.
Servers, storage and networking equipment make up the Hewlett Packard Enterprise lineup, while Dell sells servers, storage and PCs. Super Micro Computer builds AI-optimized servers, giving it a more direct tie to AI data center buildouts than Hewlett Packard Enterprise or Dell.
AI Financing Doubts Extend the Hardware Selloff
Pressure on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock extends a selloff in AI hardware as investors question how AI infrastructure spending gets financed. Data center buildouts demand heavy upfront expenditures. Doubts about who funds them flow straight back to the companies that sell the equipment, including Hewlett Packard Enterprise. We pulled together seven suppliers riding that same expansion, from power to cooling and networking, in a free report here.
Barclays heightened that debate on Wednesday when it cut its ratings on Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Dell to the equivalent of hold. The firm argued that businesses haven’t yet meaningfully increased their AI spending and that recent hardware revenue strength owes more to higher memory component prices.
Broader technology funds are slipping by smaller margins. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is down 2%. Large-cap tech is holding up even better (though it’s still selling off), as the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.3%.
Networking Growth Versus Component Price Risk
The upside story for Hewlett Packard Enterprise rests on AI server demand and its expanded networking business. Networking gives the company a second growth engine alongside servers, which could buffer Hewlett Packard Enterprise if AI server orders cool.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise is still integrating Juniper Networks into its networking business, so much of the payoff depends on execution. Integration work can absorb management focus at a time when hardware demand faces fresh questions.
On the bear side, slower enterprise AI spending could leave the hardware growth at Hewlett Packard Enterprise tied to component prices. Under that view, revenue could cool once memory pricing settles down, even if customer orders hold steady.
Corporate AI budgets sit at the center of this debate. Will businesses begin to lift that spending? The next test for Hewlett Packard Enterprise is whether they do so in a way that backs up its server and networking story. Clear signs of broader enterprise adoption could ease the financing worries weighing on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock.
Memory pricing is the other open variable for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, since Barclays tied much of the recent hardware revenue strength to higher component prices. Investors can watch for whether the gap between Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock and the broader technology funds (IYW and QQQ) narrows as the financing debate plays out.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise still holds a credible growth path through AI servers and its expanded networking business, but the hardware group is trading on financing doubts for now. Traders may prefer to keep their HPE share exposure small until the enterprise AI spending question resolves.

Dell Falls 8% as Barclays Cuts Rating and Target to $574; Hewlett Packard Enterprise Drops 5%, Super Micro Computer Slides 4% Barclays just pulled the rug on two of the biggest names in AI server hardware, and the selloff raises a question every enterprise tech investor needs to answer: how much AI growth is already baked into these stocks? Published October 14, 2026, 11:34am ET · 3 min read Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

Servers are the lifeblood of software systems.

© Tommy Lee Walker Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL | DELL Price Prediction) stock is down 8% to $526.86 in morning trading after Barclays cut its rating on the shares to Equal Weight from Overweight. The call questions how much more upside Wall Street can assign to a company whose artificial intelligence (AI) server business is still expanding quickly. That tension is now central to a broad pullback in enterprise hardware names tied to AI demand. Meanwhile, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) stock is down 5% to $65.45 after drawing the same downgrade from Barclays. Additionally, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 4% to $37.37, a lighter decline than Dell’s. Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells similar server and networking equipment to the same enterprise buyers, while Super Micro Computer builds comparable systems as a smaller specialist. Selling pressure is far greater in hardware than across the broader sector, as the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is down 1%. Large-cap growth benchmarks are holding up even better, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.9%, a much softer decline than the server makers are posting. Barclays Questions How Much AI Growth Is Priced In Barclays analyst Tim Long wrote that valuations across corporate-focused hardware names have run too far and that he doesn’t yet see a meaningful AI inflection in enterprise spending. Long lowered his price target on Dell stock to $574 and on Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares to $77. He still expects Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise to top earnings estimates, though he argued the scale of those surprises is likely to become much smaller. Long’s downgrade takes aim at valuation. That leaves Dell’s AI server growth outlook intact, so the real debate centers on how much good news Dell stock already reflects after its strong run. Separately, Accenture and Dell announced an expanded partnership on October 9. The deal is built around a dedicated private AI business group, aimed at customers who want to run those workloads inside their own data centers. Dell sells servers, storage and personal computers, and its recent growth has come from configuring and shipping AI computing racks built around other companies’ chips. That’s a high-volume business earning thin margins on expensive hardware. When upside surprises shrink, a business built on shipping volume has less room to impress on profitability, which can leave Dell stock more exposed to valuation concerns. Enterprise buyers sit at the core of Dell’s AI exposure, which places the company directly in the path of Long’s concern about corporate spending, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise faces a similar question because it sells into many of the same corporate data centers. Such overlap helps explain why one analyst note is weighing on shares of Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise together. The next share-price move for Dell stock could depend on whether corporate customers start ordering AI hardware at the scale its valuation already assumes. Long’s call frames that as an unresolved question. The Accenture partnership offers an early read on how quickly private AI demand takes shape (we featured seven suppliers riding the same data-center expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). A parallel question hangs over Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which sells similar equipment to the same corporate buyers. Smaller beats from Dell would support the Barclays view, while another large upside surprise would challenge it, and any visible pickup in corporate AI orders could also ease the valuation pressure Long describes. HPE and Miami HEAT transform Kaseya Center fan experience with AI-native wireless connectivity powered by an HPE Self-Driving Network
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:09 AM CDT 4 min read
New Wi-Fi 7 and next-generation autonomous networking will deliver enhanced connected experiences for fans, staff and venue operations
Miami HEAT is using HPE's AI-native networking capabilities to improve connectivity across the venue, providing enhanced digital experiences for fans and staff.
The partnership introduces HPE's self-driving network capabilities to automatically optimize performance, reduce operational burden, and simplify troubleshooting.
The modernized infrastructure provides a scalable foundation for Kaseya Center to easily adapt to future technologies.
MIAMI, October 19, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE (NYSE: HPE) and the Miami HEAT today announced a network modernization project at Kaseya Center designed to enhance connectivity and create a more intelligent, resilient digital foundation for fans, staff and venue operations. This connectivity refresh is part of a series of updates being made to the venue ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season to improve the arena experience for attendees.
As one of the NBA's premier venues, Kaseya Center hosts events attended by tens of thousands of people with changing conditions and a slew of devices that put significant demands on its network infrastructure. To deliver a consistently high-performing connected experience across the arena, the Miami HEAT selected HPE to modernize both its wireless and wired infrastructure and establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity.
The deployment combines HPE Aruba wireless outdoor and indoor access points and campus gateways with HPE Juniper switching that provides the power, bandwidth and capacity required to support high-density connectivity throughout the venue. HPE will also provide Arena Event Network Monitoring Assistance across five live events to help validate and optimize network performance under real-world conditions.
"Today's sports and entertainment venues need networks that can deliver exceptional experiences for tens of thousands of people while also simplifying operations behind the scenes," said Rami Rahim, executive vice president, president and general manager, Networking at HPE. "Together with the Miami HEAT, we're building a self-driving network at Kaseya Center that is designed to improve connectivity, increase operational efficiency and create new possibilities for digital experiences for fans and staff."
Building the foundation for a more connected Kaseya Center
The project began with the Miami HEAT seeking to improve wireless performance in high-density areas of Kaseya Center, particularly the lower bowl. Through technical assessment and design, the effort expanded beyond a wireless refresh to include modernization of the underlying wired infrastructure required to support next-generation access points.
The new HPE networking infrastructure will help the Miami HEAT:
Deliver a Wi-Fi 7 experience for fans and staff across Kaseya Center
Improve wireless reliability and performance in high-density and critical seating areas
Provide the power and bandwidth required for next-generation wireless access points
Establish a modern network foundation that can support future digital experiences and venue innovation
Optimize performance during live events with self-driving operations, specialized network monitoring and tuning services
"Providing a reliable, seamless digital experience for everyone who enters Kaseya Center is critical, and important to us to ensure the best possible fan experience whether attending a HEAT game, a concert or another live event," said Drew Dorben, Vice President and CTO of the Miami HEAT. "With HPE, we're modernizing our digital foundation to better serve fans and staff today and into the future."
Advancing toward AI-driven, self-driving network operations
HPE's AI-native networking capabilities are designed to help organizations move from reactive network management toward increasingly autonomous operations. HPE's self-driving network uses AI-driven insights and automation to proactively identify and resolve connectivity issues, optimize performance and simplify troubleshooting, which helps IT teams maintain reliable connectivity while reducing the operational burden of managing increasingly complex environments.
For a high-density venue such as Kaseya Center, this approach provides the Miami HEAT with a scalable foundation to support evolving connectivity demands across basketball games, concerts and other major events.
The wireless deployment is expected to be completed ahead of the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season, with the broader campus switching modernization continuing in phases across the venue.
HPE is working with AT&T, which will provide communication services and CSPi Technology Solutions that will provide implementation expertise and ongoing managed IT services to support the networking environment.

We empower our customers across industries to optimize operational performance, transform data into foresight, and maximize their impact. Unlock your boldest ambitions with HPE. Pre-Market Stock Futures:
Futures are trading mostly higher after a rather ho-hum start to the third-quarter earnings season. Large-cap financial stocks led off with strong numbers, though the sector’s results were mixed. JPMorgan Chase & Company (NYSE: JPM | JPM Price Prediction) reported strong results, but the firm’s fixed-income trading was down for the first time in two years, while Citigroup (NYSE: C) posted its best third-quarter revenue in a decade, as profits jumped 40% year-over-year, driven by a 6% rise in trading revenue. By Tuesday’s close, all major indices were modestly lower, with the small-cap Russell 2000 down the most, closing at 2,783, down 0.40%, while the Dow Jones Industrials fell 0.35% to 51,670. The tech-heavy Nasdaq closed down only 0.15% at 27,204 despite heavy selling in the chip sector, and the S&P 500 closed Tuesday’s session almost unchanged at 7,805, down only 0.02%.
Treasury Bonds:
After a day off for the Columbus Day holiday, bond markets returned to action Tuesday, with mixed trading as yields rose in shorter maturities and T-bills. In comparison, buyers eyed the belly of the curve and longer maturities, where yields were lower. By the close, the 30-year bond yield stood at 5.66%, while the 10-year note was last seen at 5.22%.
Oil and Gas:
Prices were mixed across the energy complex as heightened tensions across the Middle East continue to grow, with Saudi Arabia furious over the Houthi weekend attack on the Riyadh airport that killed 14 and wounded over 300, vowing a strong military resposne. Brent Crude closed Tuesday’s session at $106.10, down 0.48%, while West Texas Intermediate was last seen at $94.14, up 0.40%. Natural gas roared back from a slow start to the week, closing Tuesday at $3.28, up 3.66%.
Gold:
Gold was modestly lower on Tuesday; a stronger dollar, higher yields, and concerns over upcoming inflation data weighed on the bullion after a strong Monday. At the close, Gold was at $4,160, while Silver was last seen at $9.05, down 1.84%.

Because crypto never sleeps and trades 24/7, Bitcoin dipped sharply to an early low near $81,000 before staging a rapid comeback, surging back over $84,000 Tuesday afternoon and ultimately stabilizing around $83,300 to $83,500 later in the day. Ryder Cup tech spotlight and AI data center win put Hewlett Packard Enterprise in focus
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has drawn fresh attention after a US$1.2 billion AMD Helios AI Rack order from Vultr and plans to run self-driving networking at the 2027 Ryder Cup in Ireland.
Recent trading suggests investors are treating Hewlett Packard Enterprise as an AI infrastructure and networking story rather than a slow-moving hardware vendor. The 1-month share price return of 38.63% and year-to-date share price gain of 198.26% point to strong momentum, while a 1-year total shareholder return of 181.39% and 5-year total shareholder return of 460.84% show that confidence has been building over multiple years as new deals and headline events, such as the Vultr contract and Ryder Cup partnership, have landed.

Strategic acquisitions and expansion in high-growth technologies, including the integration of Juniper, launches of next-gen Gen12 servers, and AI-driven management platforms, are enhancing HPE's competitive positioning in edge, networking, and AI, laying the groundwork for continued share gains and outsized revenue growth relative to traditional industry averages.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Stock Gets Fair Value Bump As Analysts Split On AI Momentum
The fair value estimate for Hewlett Packard Enterprise has shifted from US$65.56 to US$68.08, a modest change that still matters if you are tracking valuation closely. This tweak reflects a divided analyst view, with supportive commentary pointing to strong server, cloud and AI orders, and more cautious voices focusing on networking supply constraints and the sharp share price move earlier in 2026. As you read on, you will see how to follow this evolving Hewlett Packard Enterprise narrative and what to watch next in the research.
Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Hewlett Packard Enterprise.
Several firms, including Citi, Barclays, BofA, Raymond James, Truist, Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank, have raised price targets on Hewlett Packard Enterprise, citing strong Q3 results, Cloud and AI order strength, and higher guidance for FY26 and FY27.
Networking is a key focus in recent research. Morgan Stanley and Barclays highlight networking as an important earnings driver, supported by AI demand, new products and expected Juniper synergies.
Wells Fargo and Citi comment on record or robust backlog and multi year supply commitments, which they indicate support visibility on future revenue and free cash flow for Hewlett Packard Enterprise.
Deutsche Bank notes that roughly two thirds of HPE's reported US$6.3b AI backlog is in enterprise and sovereign customers, which it characterizes as attractive for higher margin networking attach and software or integration opportunities.
Evercore ISI recently downgraded Hewlett Packard Enterprise to In Line, citing valuation following a very large year to date share price gain and fewer near term catalysts for further multiple expansion.
Evercore ISI and Piper Sandler flag networking supply constraints and concerns about the company meeting demand, with Piper Sandler also questioning how exposed HPE is to the areas of end market strength and raising the risk of peaking revenue and margins.

The fair value estimate for Hewlett Packard Enterprise has changed from US$65.56 to US$68.08.
The revenue growth assumption has shifted from about 12.90% to roughly 13.84%.
The net profit margin assumption is now about 9.81%, compared with roughly 8.55% previously.
The future P/E assumption has moved from about 24.07x to roughly 19.12x.
The discount rate has changed from 9.43% to about 9.23%.

HOUSTON, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE today announced HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon1. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery," said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. "With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration."

HPE reports fiscal 2026 third quarter results
Record results and demand drive higher outlook for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027
-Record revenue of $12.2 billion, up 34% year-over-year
-Record operating profit, with GAAP OP up 464% and non-GAAP OP up 155% year-over-year
HOUSTON – September 2, 2026 – HPE (NYSE: HPE) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended July 31, 2026.
“HPE’s strategy is proving itself again this quarter. Our results demonstrate the durability of our profitable growth momentum. We delivered record revenue, orders, and profitability, fueled by surging customer demand across our portfolio,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE. “AI is becoming a multi-year growth driver for HPE, and our differentiated portfolio positions us to capture that opportunity at scale.”
“Our outstanding revenue performance and expanded profitability in the third quarter reflect robust demand across our portfolio and consistent, disciplined execution,” said Marie Myers, executive vice president and CFO of HPE. “With our Q3 results and our order backlog at a record level, we are raising our financial outlook and plan to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4.”
Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results
•Revenue: $12.2 billion, up 34% from the prior-year period
•Gross margins:
◦GAAP of 40.1%, up 1,090 basis points from the prior-year period and up 360 basis points sequentially
◦Non-GAAP(1) of 40.4%, up 1,050 basis points from the prior-year period and up 350 basis points sequentially
•Operating profit margins:
◦GAAP of 11.4%, up 870 basis points from the prior-year period and up 440 basis points sequentially
◦Non-GAAP(1) of 16.2%, up 770 basis points from the prior-year period and up 290 basis points sequentially
•Diluted net earnings per share (“EPS”):
◦GAAP of $1.06, up $0.85 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.84 - $0.89
◦Non-GAAP(1) of $1.11, up $0.67 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.88 - $0.93
•Cash flow from operations: $1.6 billion, an increase of $0.3 billion from the prior-year period
•Free cash flow(1)(2): $1.0 billion, an increase of $0.2 billion from the prior-year period
•Capital returns to common shareholders: $324 million in the form of dividends and share repurchases
Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Segment Results
•Networking revenue was $2.9 billion, up 74.9% from the prior-year period, with 22.0% operating profit margin, compared to 22.1% from the prior-year period.
◦Within Networking, revenue from:
▪Campus & Branch was $1.4 billion, up 31.0% from the prior-year period.
▪Data Center Networking was $382 million, up 112.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Security was $281 million, up 75.6% from the prior-year period.
▪Routing was $788 million, up 270.0% from the prior-year period.
•Cloud & AI revenue was $9.0 billion, up 25.4% from the prior-year period, with 17.0% operating profit margin, compared to 7.0% from the prior-year period.
◦Within Cloud & AI, revenue from:
▪Server was $6.8 billion, up 35.3% from the prior-year period.
▪Storage was $1.3 billion, up 10.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Financial Services was $0.9 billion, down 0.3% from the prior-year period.
•Corporate Investments and Other revenue was $278 million, up 3.0% from the prior-year period, with -24.1% of operating profit margin, compared to -7.0% from the prior-year period.
The HPE Board of Directors declared a regular cash dividend of $0.1425 per share on the company’s common stock, payable on or about October 16, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 17, 2026.
HPE estimates revenue to be in the range of $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion. HPE estimates GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $1.12 to $1.22 and non-GAAP diluted net EPS(1) to be in the range of $1.20 to $1.30. Fiscal 2026 fourth quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimate excludes net after-tax
adjustments of approximately $0.08 per diluted share, primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, and cost reduction program.
HPE is raising its FY26 revenue growth outlook range to 34% to 37%. HPE is raising revenue growth expectations for the Networking segment to 73% to 74%. HPE estimates GAAP operating profit growth range to be 1,070% to 1,105% and non-GAAP operating profit growth range between 100% to 105%(1)(3).
HPE is raising both GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $2.93 to $3.03 and non-GAAP diluted net EPS(1) to be in the range of $3.75 to $3.85. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimate excludes net after-tax adjustments of approximately $0.82 per diluted share, primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, cost reduction program, and adjustments related to the sale of H3C. HPE is also raising its free cash flow(1)(2)(4) guidance and now expects free cash flow to be at least $3.75 billion.
The company is raising its growth framework for FY27. HPE is raising its revenue growth outlook range to 13% to 17%. HPE is raising expectations for non-GAAP diluted net EPS growth to be in the range of 16% to 20%(1)(4). HPE estimates non-GAAP operating margin rate to be in the range of 14% to 15%(1)(4). HPE is also raising its free cash flow guidance and now expects free cash flow to be at least $5.0 billion(1)(2)(4).
1 A description of HPE’s use of non-GAAP financial information is provided below under “Use of non-GAAP financial information and key performance metrics.”
2 Free cash flow represents cash flow from operations, less net capital expenditures (investments in property, plant & equipment (“PP&E”) and software assets less proceeds from the sale of PP&E), and adjusted for the effect of exchange rate fluctuations on cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash.
3 FY26 non-GAAP operating profit excludes costs of approximately $2.5 billion primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, and cost reduction program.
4 HPE provides certain guidance on a non-GAAP basis. In reliance on the exception provided by Item 10(e)(1)(i)(B) of Regulation S-K, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is unable to provide a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure without unreasonable efforts, as the Company cannot predict some elements that are included in such directly comparable GAAP financial measure. These elements could have a material impact on the Company’s reported GAAP results for the guidance period. Refer to the discussion of non-GAAP financial measures below for more information.
HPE (NYSE: HPE) is a leader in essential enterprise technology, bringing together the power of AI, cloud, and networking to help organizations achieve more. As pioneers of possibility, our innovation and expertise advance the way people live and work. We empower our customers across industries to
optimize operational performance, transform data into foresight, and maximize their impact. Unlock your boldest ambitions with HPE. Discover more at www.hpe.com.

Investor Contact:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise also provides forecasts of non-GAAP operating profit growth, non-GAAP diluted net earnings per share, and FCF. HPE just posted its worst week ever after a single analyst downgrade, yet its earnings are surging and its backlog hit a record high. Published October 20, 2026, 7:31am ET · 4 min read Two professionals analyze market data and financial trends on a laptop, mirroring the optimistic outlook and raised price targets for companies like HPE. © VideoFlow / Shutterstock.com Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) fell 20.56% in the week through October 19. It was its worst week ever, following an October 14 analyst downgrade that questioned HPE’s AI growth. The drop hit a stock that already traded at a forward PE of roughly 12 to 15, while the broader market averages 30. Investors Dave Ahern and Stephen Morris recently debated whether that gap makes HPE an opportunity or a value trap. Ahern asked: “Is that a lifetime opportunity, or does Wall Street know something that the rest of value investors maybe don’t know? Like, why is it so cheap?” The question is pressing because the results are strong. Revenue in the fiscal third quarter rose 32.7% to $12.21 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the $0.93 consensus. Morris rated HPE’s moat today as “next to non-existent,” and that view accounts for most of the discount. A 12x Multiple Signals Doubt About Durability A forward PE divides the share price by expected earnings. A low multiple therefore means investors doubt those estimates will hold, and the market is currently pricing in a fade in AI server demand. The trailing P/E of 1300x is distorted by Juniper integration charges and a fiscal 2025 goodwill impairment. That is why the hosts focus on the forward number. Analysts’ average fiscal 2027 EPS estimate is $4.7088, up from $4.0384 90 days ago. None of those analysts revised down in the past 30 days. Management’s own fiscal 2027 framework calls for EPS of $4.40 to $4.60. That range leaves out the Helios AI rack opportunity. Wall Street Turned Cautious After a Huge Run Even after falling 8.05% over the past month, HPE is still up 135.22% year to date and 147.52% over the past year. Shares rose 1.29% on October 19 to $55.84. The post-downgrade rebound was small. Although the market has embraced HPE this year, it remains unclear whether AI-driven earnings will last long enough to justify that price. Still, orders grew faster than revenue, and backlog hit a record while memory shortages held back shipments. Ahern’s long-term test sets the hype aside: “Forget the AI trade. What is a stock going to do 10 years from now?” AI server revenue fails that test because it is cyclical: orders shrink once data center buildouts slow, and nothing ties buyers to HPE. Miami HEAT selected HPE to modernize both its wireless and wired infrastructure and establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity. This connectivity refresh is part of a series of updates being made to the venue ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season to improve the arena experience for attendees. The deployment combines HPE Aruba wireless outdoor and indoor access points and campus gateways with HPE Juniper switching that provides the power, bandwidth and capacity required to support high-density connectivity throughout the venue.
HPE will also provide Arena Event Network Monitoring Assistance across five live events to help validate and optimize network performance under real-world conditions. HPE?s AI-native networking capabilities are designed to help organizations move from reactive network management toward increasingly autonomous operations. HPE?s self-driving network uses AI-driven insights and automation to proactively identify and resolve connectivity issues, optimize performance and simplify troubleshooting, which helps IT teams maintain reliable connectivity while reducing the operational burden of managing increasingly complex environments.
For a high-density venue such as Kaseya Center, this approach provides the Miami HEAT with a scalable foundation to support evolving connectivity demands across basketball games, concerts and other major events. The wireless deployment is expected to be completed ahead of the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season, with the broader campus switching modernization continuing in phases across the venue. HPE is working with AT&T, which will provide communication services and CSPi Technology Solutions that will provide implementation expertise and ongoing managed IT services to support the networking environment.

HOUSTON, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE today announced HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon1. The system will deploy on Astrolab's FLIP rover for an upcoming mission for the Moon Base program and will test the suitability of advanced computing for future missions and the emerging lunar economy.
"For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world's most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery," said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. "With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration."
The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. facts.text: HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 will power AI and first HPC benchmarks on the Moon's surface using Astrolab's FLIP rover for NASA's Moon Base program mission.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 tests LLM retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, and LiDAR data for lunar AI deployment.
The mission plans to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA's CLPS initiative with Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lander transporting the payload.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is a lightweight, fanless compute module with CPU and GPU designed for lunar South Pole environment.
NASA and Deloitte will deploy AI workloads on HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 to maximize scientific discovery and lunar economy infrastructure.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 uses KIOXIA flash storage and HPE CloudOps Software for lunar mission management.
HPE's revenue in the fiscal third quarter rose 32.7% to $12.21 billion.
HPE's non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the $0.93 consensus for the fiscal third quarter.
HPE's shares fell 20.56% in the week through October 19, marking its worst week ever.
HPE's fiscal 2027 EPS estimate is $4.7088, up from $4.0384 90 days ago.
HPE's Juniper Networks acquisition and sale of its remaining 19% stake in H3C in May 2026 shifted its business mix toward networking.
HPE's networking revenue jumped 74.9% to $2.89 billion, with orders rising 36%.
HPE's GreenLake service reached 52,000 customers, up 18%.
HPE's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 will run high-performance LINPACK (HPL) and high-performance conjugate gradient (HPCG) benchmarks on the Moon's surface.
HPE has secured a $1.2 billion deal with Vultr for AMD Helios technology.
Firefly Aerospace has signed Starcloud as a commercial customer for data center capabilities around the Moon.
HPE was selected for R&D projects by the U.S. DOE-led Genesis Mission to advance AI-driven innovation and scientific discovery.
Orbital was selected by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to deploy AI software for Earth science applications.
IBM and NASA released an open-source AI model for lunar exploration.
Vultr selected HPE and NVIDIA for next-generation AI infrastructure for cloud-scale data centers.
HPE has shattered its 52-week high on a single session surge.
HPE's forward P/E ratio is 12x with 400% growth expectations.
Dell Technologies' stock has risen over 250% year to date.
HPE surged while its closest AI server rivals barely moved due to a single deal.
HPE's shares have risen 80.25% year to date.
HPE raised its guidance and posted blockbuster growth but the stock is sinking.
Super Micro's stock climbed 4% while HPE advanced 5%.
HPE's margin beat has a built-in expiration date acknowledged by management.
Miami Heat selected HPE to modernize wireless and wired infrastructure at Kaseya Center with Wi-Fi 7 connectivity ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season.
Miami Heat selected HPE to modernize wireless and wired infrastructure at Kaseya Center for 2026-2027 NBA season with Wi-Fi 7 connectivity, using HPE Aruba wireless and Juniper switching solutions.
HPE stock gained 1.29% to close at $55.84 on Monday, October 19, following Miami HEAT's selection of HPE for Wi-Fi 7 upgrade at Kaseya Center.
HPE will test and optimize network performance across five live events to ensure reliability during high-traffic scenarios.
The project aims to address high-density wireless needs at Kaseya Center by upgrading both wireless access and wired infrastructure.
HPE plans to use AI-assisted network tools to identify faults and improve performance during the Kaseya Center rollout.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise launched HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers with 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, featuring higher core density, expanded memory/I/O, and security features like automatic self encrypting drives and post quantum cryptography readiness.
HPE ProLiant Gen13 targets AI inference, agentic AI workflows, data intensive simulations, and financial modeling for customers modernizing data centers and hybrid cloud environments.
Mizuho Securities deployed HPE Cray XD2000 with direct liquid cooling, linking to HPE's ProLiant Gen13 servers for high density, liquid cooled compute for AI training/inference workloads.
Consensus forecasts project HPE revenue to grow 14.3% annually over three years, reaching US$62.5b by 2029, with earnings rising from US$2.7b to US$6.1b.
Analysts project HPE's margins to expand from 6.4% to 9.8% in three years through AI infrastructure, data center networking, and recurring GreenLake services.
